gloss: to feel ashamed; to be embarrassed

definitions.gloss: to feel ashamed; to be embarrassed; to feel disgrace
definitions.explanation: To feel shame about one's own actions, behavior, or shortcomings. A more introspective and literary word than 恥ずかしい.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{無知|むち}を{恥|は}じた。
examples.english: I felt ashamed of my own ignorance.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}の{失敗|しっぱい}を{恥|は}じることはない。
examples.english: There's no need to be ashamed of past mistakes.

examples.japanese: {先輩|せんぱい}の{前|まえ}で{恥|は}じるような{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}いをしてしまった。
examples.english: I behaved in a way I was ashamed of in front of my senior.

notes:
GRAMMAR:
Ichidan verb ({一段動詞|いちだんどうし}), intransitive. Takes を to mark what one is ashamed of: ～を{恥|は}じる.

USAGE:
More formal and reflective than {恥|は}ずかしい. Used when someone feels genuine shame about their own conduct or character, not simply situational embarrassment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自分|じぶん}を{恥|は}じる (to be ashamed of oneself)
- {無知|むち}を{恥|は}じる (to be ashamed of one's ignorance)
- {恥|は}じることなく (without shame; shamelessly)
- {恥|は}じ{入|い}る (to be deeply ashamed)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {恥|は}ずかしい: embarrassing; embarrassed — covers both situational embarrassment and shame, much more common in daily conversation
- {恥|は}じ{入|い}る: to be deeply ashamed — stronger, more literary form
